caption: Newanforbi v. United Parcel Service, Inc.
claims: PC §290.46(j)(2)(E) Violation, Failure to Hire (Tameny), ICRAA, Invasion of Privacy, Negligence Per Se, UCL §17200

causes: Failure to Hire in Violation of Public Policy (Tameny)
Violation of ICRAA (Cal. Civ. Code § 1786 et seq.)
Invasion of Privacy (Cal. Const., Art. I, § 1)
Unlawful Business Practices (Bus. & Prof. Code § 17200 et seq.)
key_facts: In or around mid-2024, Plaintiff applied for a position in UPS's delivery and logistics operations in California. As part of its standard pre-employment screening, UPS initiated a background check through First Advantage (fadv.com). On July 22, 2024 at 9:57 AM, Plaintiff received a 'Pre Adverse Action Notification regarding your application with UPS' from First Advantage (DoNotReply@fadv.com) directing him to review the report for 'UNITED PARCEL SERVICE' via a secure portal link. Reminder notices followed on July 23, 2024 (10:00 AM) and July 27, 2024 (10:00 AM). On July 31, 2024 at 9:57 AM — nine days after the original pre-adverse notice — Plaintiff received a 'Final Adverse Action Notification regarding your application with UPS,' confirming UPS had taken final adverse action, definitively denying him employment. UPS provided no written communication identifying any basis for the denial other than the background screening report; no other disqualifying information existed in Plaintiff's application. Plaintiff is a registrant on California's Megan's Law sex offender registry, and alleges on information and belief that the First Advantage report disclosed that status to UPS (together with a statutory disclaimer warning that the information could not lawfully be used for employment purposes) and that UPS used it as the basis for the denial, in violation of Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E).
procedural_status: Complaint filed July 15, 2026 (San Joaquin Sup. Ct. STK-CV-UWT-2026-0009113); FW-003 granted; served July 22, 2026 on UPS via Sacramento County Sheriff. REMOVED Aug. 20, 2026 and assigned the same day to USDC E.D. Cal., Sacramento Division, as No. 2:26-cv-02847-DAD-CKD (PS). Nature of suit coded 442 Civil Rights: Jobs; jurisdiction Diversity; jury demand Both. Docket as of Aug. 20, 2026: Dkt. 1 Notice of Removal (fee $405, receipt ACAEDC-13761260, with civil cover sheet, Felsing declaration, and Rule 7.1 statement); Dkt. 2 Civil New Case Documents / Initial Scheduling Order signed by M.J. Delaney, plus Dkt. 2-1 magistrate-consent materials, served on Plaintiff by mail; Dkt. 3 UPS certificate of service attesting service of the removal papers on Plaintiff by mail at 1455 Cat Tail Drive on Aug. 20, 2026. UPS's counsel of record is Vanessa W. Mott alone, at 5800 Armada Drive, Suite 101, Carlsbad — not the Costa Mesa address on the removal papers; Alyssa R. Daskas is not on the docket. UPS's certificate lists Plaintiff's email as 'Bnn.cdla@gmail.com', which is wrong (bnn.cdl@gmail.com); service was by mail so no prejudice, but correct it at the first opportunity. INITIAL SCHEDULING ORDER terms: because this is a removed action, footnote 1 puts the service obligation on UPS — it must serve the order and the consent form on Plaintiff and file a notice of that service; the 90-day Rule 4(m) service duty in paragraph 2 does not run against Plaintiff. If UPS responds by motion, it notices the hearing under L.R. 230(b) and Plaintiff's opposition is due 14 days after the motion is FILED (L.R. 230(c)) — failure to oppose may be taken as consent to granting it — while Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(a)(1)(B) allows one amendment as of right within 21 days of service of a Rule 12(b), (e) or (f) motion. If UPS answers, the parties confer under Rule 26 within 30 days and file a joint status report 7 days later. Consent/Decline of magistrate jurisdiction to be filed as soon as practicable. Neither Plaintiff's Aug. 20 Notice of Errata nor the Aug. 21 Amended Notice was filed — both were mooted by the Sacramento assignment and the correct docket caption. UPS filed a Rule 12(b)(6) motion Aug. 26, 2026 (ECF Nos. 7, 7-1, 7-2, 7-3), noticed for Oct. 5, 2026, 1:30 p.m.; Drozd civil L&M is Zoom (Standing Order I.A). Plaintiff's opposition is on file as Dkt. 10 (FILED Aug. 28, 2026). Drozd Standing Order I.E: the proposed order stays unfiled unless the Court asks. Rule 15(a)(1)(B) amendment-as-of-right window is Sep. 16, possibly Sep. 19 under Rule 6(d) for mail service. Dated beats live in timeline.json. On September 1, 2026 Plaintiff mailed federal papers First-Class from San Jose (USPS eReceipt on Matter 19); a magistrate-consent copy is believed to be in that batch and remains unfiled until clerk-stamped. No PACER docket number yet Plaintiff's Consent to Magistrate Judge Jurisdiction (dated September 1, 2026; POS by mail from San Jose) is executed and unfiled. File with the Sacramento clerk (L.R. 305). On September 4, 2026 UPS telephoned and asked for a 30-day extension of its reply, then a 15-day extension; Plaintiff declined both. No stipulation. E.D. Cal. L.R. 230(d) runs the reply from the opposition filing date, not the hearing: 10 days after Dkt. 10 (Aug. 28) is Monday, Sep. 7 (Labor Day), rolled to Tuesday, Sep. 8 under Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(1)(C). A 15-day extension would have run to Sep. 23. A 30-day extension would have run to Oct. 8, after the Oct. 5 hearing. Clock and hearing unchanged. Same day UPS filed Dkt. 11 (captioned Consent; paragraph 4 admits no consent; asks through Sep. 14). Plaintiff's opposition executed the same day; unfiled until clerk-stamped. PACER Sep. 4: UPS declined MJ jurisdiction (Dkt. 5); Dkt. 8 vacated the Oct. 5 Drozd hearing; live MTD is Dkt. 9 (Oct. 7, 10:00 a.m., Courtroom 24, Judge Delaney).
damages: Statutory civil remedy under PC § 290.46(j)(4)(A): actual damages, up to treble and not less than $250, plus attorney's fees and exemplary damages, or a civil penalty not exceeding $25,000 — the $25,000 figure is a cap on the civil penalty, not a floor alternative to actual damages. CONSERVATIVE: civil-penalty cap plus modest actuals/emotional distress (no W-2; never hired). MODERATE: ~$85,000 (actuals/treble, ICRAA, emotional distress, fee-shifting). AGGRESSIVE: ~$200,000 if discovery confirms willful registry-based denial and supports Civil Code § 3294 punitives. UPS Exhibit A is now in the record; the remaining fight is statutory construction and use, not whether the report exists.
risk: Merits posture unchanged by removal — a federal court sitting in diversity applies the same California substantive law. PC §290.46(j)(2)(E) still bars employment use. UPS's live defenses are a 'national not California' reading of Exhibit A and a (j)(3)→Labor Code 432.7(n) savings-clause argument. UPS lodged the First Advantage report and does not dispute it used the background check to deny hire (ECF 7 at 3). The only Decisional / INELIGIBLE component is the NSOR hit whose Sentence field reads SOURCE OF RECORD: CALIFORNIA SEX OFFENDER REGISTRY. Count I is the load-bearing claim; Williams knocks the Tameny label on Count II, not the statutory private right of action. Negligence per se (Count V) is a doctrine, not a COA (Dent). REMAND: not worth filing. UPS's own amount-in-controversy math concedes the point is close — $21/hr x 16 hrs/wk x 179 weeks = $60,144, below the $75,000 threshold, and its ¶34 says a conservative estimate only 'nearly exceeds' it — and its future-attorney's-fee theory for a pro se plaintiff is unsupported by any evidence, contrary to Fritsch v. Swift Transp. Co. of Ariz., LLC, 899 F.3d 785, 794-95 (9th Cir. 2018). But Plaintiff's own July 12, 2026 pre-filing demand of $85,000 is admissible evidence of the amount in controversy under Cohn v. PetSmart, Inc., 281 F.3d 837, 840 (9th Cir. 2002), and the PC §290.46(j)(4)(A) civil penalty (capped at $25,000, plus actual damages, fees, and exemplary damages) stacks on top of the $60,144 wage figure. A remand motion loses and costs a month. UPSIDE OF REMOVAL: Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(1) initial disclosures and Rule 45 reach the First Advantage report without a demurrer cycle; UPS has demanded a jury; and a 15 U.S.C. §1681b(b)(3)(A) FCRA claim — already supported by the pre-adverse/final-adverse notices in evidence — is now natively at home here and carries real fee-shifting under §§1681n-1681o, which is the fee theory that actually works for a pro se plaintiff. DOWNSIDE: the Aug. 26 MTD leads with Tameny/Williams and the national-registry construction. Count I does not need a FAC to survive; the opposition is on file as Dkt. 10. A FAC by Sep. 16 is a pleading tool, not a calendar tool. On punitives, the Aug. 17 §425.115 notice sets nothing in federal court; a punitive award still requires evidence of UPS's financial condition (Adams v. Murakami (1991) 54 Cal.3d 105).
